text:
kevin-platform: FYI - OrchardHealth asked for a temporary per-org routing override to send traffic to dedicated-east-qa overnight for an integration test. They want it for 2 weeks. Any objections?

maria-eng: can we do this purely via a routing header + allowlist? `X-Org-Routing: orchard-east` 

jess-product: they need auditability and an expiration. product prefers an admin toggle in Console + an email to the account owner.

kevin-platform: agree on audit + expiry. question: should this bypass the normal routing policy matching or be implemented as a higher-priority rule?

maria-eng: implement as higher-priority rule that is evaluated before default matchers. i.e. routing rules order: org-overrides -> customer-allowlist -> global routes -> fallback.

alex-sre: also we must preserve quota semantics. Dedicated pool shouldn't let them exceed committed capacity silently. add `quota_scope: org` and surface usage in the Console.

kevin-platform: good point. we need to decide whether billing/quotas follow the org or the target pool.

jess-product: billing stays with customer org. target pool capacity is just a routing destination. if pool full, fallback to hosted with warning.

maria-eng: example rule syntax we could store in config DB: 

```
- id: override-orchard-east-nightly
  priority: 10
  match: 
    headers:
      X-Org-Override: orchard-east
    time_window: '22:00-06:00'
  action:
    route_to: dedicated-east-qa
    audit: true
    expires_at: '2026-04-10T06:00:00Z'
```

kevin-platform: Nice. Two implementation concerns: header spoofing and admin approval flow.

duncan-ops: header spoofing -> require HMAC signed header `X-Override-Signature` verified by gateway. we already use similar HMAC for escape-hatch.

maria-eng: +1. also strip override headers before forwarding to backend for security.

alex-sre: telemetry: emit `route_override_applied` metric with tags {org_id, rule_id, routed_pool}. also increment `override_failures` when signature fails. keep sample log line: 

```
level=info event=route_override_applied org=orchard id=override-orchard-east-nightly target=dedicated-east-qa src_ip=10.2.3.4
```

jess-product: Console UX: add a modal in Account > Routing -> Overrides. fields: target pool, start/end, time windows, approve (checkbox), reason, audit contact. show recent overrides + audit link.

kevin-platform: approvals: require at least one approver from Security or Platform for any override that routes to Dedicated or Private. auto-approve for Hosted pool requests below 10k tokens/day.

maria-eng: ops-bot can create a PR-like change request object stored in config service. flow: request -> approver review -> activate -> ops-bot posts audit entry.

ops-bot: automation: created request #R-2026-94 for OrchardHealth. reviewers: @alex-sre, @duncan-ops.

duncan-ops: one more: we need an admin API to revoke in emergency + an escape hatch that routes back to fallback. include `force_revoke` with signed reason stored in audit.

kevin-platform: agree. also add a UI timeline for each override: created, approved, activated, revoked.

maria-eng: on the implementation side i can prototype gateway matcher and header verification this week. will raise a short RFC with sample config and DB schema.

jess-product: i'll sketch the Console mock and approval flows, send to @kevin-platform and @alex-sre for review.

kevin-platform: ok let's keep the default behavior conservative: no override applied until approved. do quick staging test for OrchardHealth with expiration set. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

alex-sre: will add telemetry + alerts: if >5% of org traffic hits overrides unexpectedly, alert SRE.

maria-eng: noted. i'll put a feature-flag behind `org_routing_overrides` and wire tests.

kevin-platform: timeline: prototype + RFC by EOW, staging rollout next week, production after approvals.

jess-product: cc finance - confirm billing attribution plan.

kevin-platform: tagging finance.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to staging for `org-routing-proto` at 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z

kevin-platform: thanks, closing thread for now.
